profile.summary: NuFold predicts the full-atom 3D structure of a single RNA chain from its sequence. It takes the sequence, a multiple sequence alignment and a predicted secondary structure, and outputs ranked structure models as PDB files. It adapts the AlphaFold2 network to RNA, with a nucleobase-centred representation that lets the ribose ring take flexible shapes.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract, Results (overview); README: Running NuFold

summary_quotes.text: NuFold is a deep neural network trained end-to-end for the output structure from the input sequence. NuFold incorporates a nucleobase center representation, which enables flexible conformation of ribose rings.
For an input RNA sequence, an MSA is generated by rMSA
NuFold shares the basic framework of deep learning architecture as AF2
Your result will be found at `test_output/2DER_C/2DER_C_rank_1.pdb`.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: NuFold keeps the three-part AlphaFold2 layout. An input module reads the sequence, an MSA from the rMSA pipeline and a secondary structure predicted by IPknot. Evoformer blocks embed the MSA and pairwise information. A structure module builds the 3D model, and the steps are repeated in recycling rounds to refine it. Instead of amino acids, the network uses seven letter types: the four nucleotides, unknown, gap and masked. The network predicts the translation and rotation of each base frame plus a set of torsion angles, which the nucleobase centre representation turns into full-atom coordinates. Training added self-distillation data from bpRNA-1m to the small set of PDB structures.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, NuFold overview and Fig. 1; Methods

quotes.text: the first module, which deals with input data, the second module, the Evoformer blocks, which generates embeddings of the multiple sequence alignments (MSA) collected for the target sequence and residue pairwise information, and the last module, the structure module, which constructs the three-dimensional (3D) structure models of the target RNA
These processes are iteratively performed in a recycling process to refine predictions.
Instead of amino acids, NuFold considers 4 + 3 letter types, which are four standard nucleotides, unknown, gaps, and masked position.
The network predicts two key components for full-atom structure prediction: the translation and rotation of the base frame, along with a set of torsion angles derived from the base frame.
dataset for a self-distillation dataset, which was combined with the training dataset during training

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README publishes one checkpoint, global_step145245.pt, downloaded from kiharalab.org, and runs it with the config preset initial_training. The paper also describes variants trained for analysis, such as smaller 24-block Evoformer models and models trained with less self-distillation data; the README does not publish these. The code is archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.14498624). NuFold was trained with PyTorch 1.10.0+cu111 and tested with 2.0.1+cu117. A result should name the commit, the checkpoint file and the MSA source, because the paper reports that metagenome MSAs and more recycling change accuracy; this page read commit f77d34af.

strengths.text: Predicts all atoms directly, and the nucleobase centre representation allows flexible ribose ring conformations. The authors report a particular advantage in correct local geometry.

quotes.text: NuFold exhibited a particular advantage in building correct local geometries of RNA.
which enables flexible conformation of ribose rings

strengths.text: Available as source code and as a Google Colab notebook, so a structure can be predicted without a local install.

quotes.text: NuFold is made available in the forms of source code and a Google Colab Notebook

strengths.text: The authors report that NuFold outperformed energy-based methods and was comparable with other deep learning methods on their benchmark.

quotes.text: Benchmark study showed that NuFold clearly outperformed energy-based methods and demonstrated comparable results with existing state-of-the-art deep-learning-based methods.

limitations.text: Needs an MSA. Setting up the rMSA database takes about 2 TB of disk and hours, and building one MSA can take a couple of hours to half a day. The paper reports worse results for shallow MSAs. The Colab version uses a quicker rMSA.

run_guide.summary: Install NuFold and its third-party tools, download the checkpoint, build the inputs for the bundled 2DER_C example and predict its structure.
prerequisites: Tested on Ubuntu 22.04 with an x86_64 CPU and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24GB GPU; VRAM needs depend on RNA length.
About 2 TB of disk for the rMSA databases, which take a few hours to set up.

steps.title: Clone the repository at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/kiharalab/NuFold.git
cd NuFold/
git checkout --detach f77d34af97c1d0f88b47dd2f3c038004fe2ebe13
steps.explanation: The clone and cd lines are from the README; the checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was written from.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/kiharalab/NuFold.git
cd NuFold/

steps.title: Create the conda environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n nufold_P python=3.10
conda activate nufold_P
pip3 install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu117
pip3 install ml-collections dm-tree deepspeed protobuf scipy biopython numpy matplotlib
steps.explanation: Creates the Python 3.10 environment with PyTorch for CUDA 11.7 and the other dependencies.

quotes.text: conda create -n nufold_P python=3.10
pip3 install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu117
pip3 install ml-collections dm-tree deepspeed protobuf scipy biopython numpy matplotlib

steps.title: Install rMSA and its databases
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/pylelab/rMSA
cd rMSA/
./database/script/update.sh
cd ../
steps.explanation: Sets up the MSA pipeline. The database step needs about 2 TB and a few hours.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/pylelab/rMSA
./database/script/update.sh

steps.title: Install IPknot
steps.shell:
wget https://github.com/satoken/ipknot/releases/download/v1.1.0/ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux.zip
unzip ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux.zip && rm ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux.zip
chmod +x ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux/ipknot
steps.explanation: Downloads the IPknot binary used for secondary structure prediction.

quotes.text: wget https://github.com/satoken/ipknot/releases/download/v1.1.0/ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux.zip
chmod +x ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux/ipknot
mkdir -p checkpoints
wget -O checkpoints/global_step145245.pt http://kiharalab.org/nufold/global_step145245.pt

steps.title: Build the MSA and secondary structure
steps.shell:
rMSA/rMSA.pl test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.fasta -cpu=32
cp test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.afa test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.a3m
ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux/ipknot test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.fasta > test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.ipknot.ss
steps.explanation: Makes the a3m and ipknot.ss inputs for the example. The MSA step can take hours; IPknot takes seconds.

quotes.text: rMSA/rMSA.pl test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.fasta -cpu=32
cp test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.afa test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.a3m
ipknot-1.1.0-x86_64-linux/ipknot test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.fasta > test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.ipknot.ss

steps.title: Run NuFold
steps.shell:
python3 run_nufold.py \
  --ckpt_path checkpoints/global_step145245.pt \
  --input_fasta test_input/2DER_C/2DER_C.fasta \
  --input_dir test_input/ \
  --output_dir test_output \
  --config_preset initial_training
steps.explanation: Predicts the structure. The README says this takes up to about 5 minutes.

quotes.text: --ckpt_path checkpoints/global_step145245.pt

notes: At the pinned commit the repository test_input/2DER_C folder holds 2DER_C.single.ipknot.ss rather than the 2DER_C.ipknot.ss the README describes, so the guide regenerates the inputs instead of reusing them. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so its bytes are not stored. The README does not state whether the GPL v3 licence covers the checkpoint. A NuFold database preprint (2026) exists but was not read.
